depth_targets.title: Scale (pricing tier)
limitations: Vyomi enforces the headline tier gates — a Basic namespace rejects topic creation and queues with sessions or duplicate detection enabled, and messaging units / premiumMessagingPartitions require a Premium namespace — but per-tier throughput, entity size and partition-COUNT limits are not otherwise modelled.

depth_targets.title: Namespace activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 7/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

depth_targets.title: Toolbar actions needing a separate Azure product or a per-row detail flyout: Activity log's Activity/Export Activity Logs/Insights/Feedback/Pin current filters, and Locks' Subscription/Resource group scope + Feedback
limitations: The per-event Activity detail flyout, continuous Export Activity Logs (to Storage/Event Hub/Log Analytics), the Insights workbook, dashboard filter-pinning and portal Feedback are not modeled.

Column customization, one-time CSV export, filtering and 'Reset to default' on both the Activity log and Locks panels ARE real (consoles/src/azure/kit/BrowseGrid.jsx, client-side over the real rows) — this entry covers only the actions listed above.

depth_targets.title: Export template (ARM template)
limitations: Only the ARM Template tab is generated from the namespace's real properties; Bicep and Terraform export are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Access control (IAM) on a namespace
limitations: Role assignments scoped to an individual resource are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Networking, Encryption and Identity
limitations: Private endpoints, customer-managed key encryption and managed identities are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Geo-disaster recovery (paired namespaces + failover)
limitations: Namespace pairing and alias failover are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Insights, Alerts, Metrics, Diagnostic settings and Logs on a namespace
limitations: Metrics charts, alert rules, diagnostic-setting log routing and Log Analytics queries are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Diagnose and solve problems, Events, Tasks, and Support + Troubleshooting
limitations: These portal troubleshooting, Event Grid integration and support tools are not modeled.

  BUILD — Vyomi can model it in the shared core (state + native API semantics): implement it in core/<svc>_core.py (and the offline route if offline lacks it), add conformance checks in tests/conformance/, raise the entry's level in core/capabilities/<cloud>/<svc>.json (not_simulated→limited/full, config_only→limited/full where now ENFORCED, limited→full where a limitation is removed), wire the console section to it with a UI↔native-API round trip in consoles/tests/smoke-<cloud>.mjs and a "live" fixture for any list/detail page.
  KEEP HONEST — only if it needs something a local simulator cannot run (a separate product, real hardware/network, billing, third-party identity): leave it NotSimulated and put the concrete reason in the entry's `limitations`.
Prefer behaviour that is ENFORCED (e.g. lifecycle rules actually expire objects, a DLQ really receives, a policy really denies) over config that is only stored. Real coverage must go UP; nothing may regress: fidelity ≥ 90%, every capability claim true on nano AND offline, smokes green. Do not edit consoles/honest-allowlist.json or .github/.
House rules: keep consoles/src/<cloud>/kit/Capability.jsx as on base (add JSON imports only), list the service ONCE in registry.js, register any NEW core in wasm/build_cores.py + wasm/nano-boot.js (own line, never inside a // comment) + core/nano_registry.py + core/nano_persist.py (tests/conformance/test_nano_core_manifest.py), unique variable names in the smoke files, 'Vyomi' as plain text, re-vendor with python3 wasm/build_cores.py, rebuild bundles, COMMIT your source.

WAVE 5 — FINISH THE GAPS (orchestrator). Work through EVERY entry in depth_targets in this order:
  1. config_only → make the stored setting TAKE EFFECT (e.g. encryption really uses our KMS / Key Vault cores; access logging really writes log objects; org-policy constraints really reject violating calls; tiering/lifecycle really moves objects; replication really copies within the simulator). Raise to limited/full.
  2. not_simulated that a simulator CAN model → build it in the shared core (state + native API + console + smoke round-trip + conformance test). Networking behaviour MUST use core/netsim (never a second evaluator).
  3. limited whose limit is only missing engine coverage (query grammar, per-request policy evaluation, missing sub-resources) → lift it.
  KEEP HONEST only: separate products (Grafana, Prometheus, Defender, Bastion, VPN/TGW/ExpressRoute, PrivateLink, Firehose without a core…), billing/payment/support, physical hardware, AI-generated insights — with the concrete reason in `limitations`.
Both substrates: every change must work on Nano (wasm cores) AND offline (check the offline route serves it — offline sometimes uses legacy provider handlers; route to the core or implement there; see core/wire_ingress.py, providers/*, routes/*). New offline state must be durable (core/appliance_stores._CoreSlotStore) and JSON-safe. Run the gate, the cloud's smoke, and the conformance tests in the FOREGROUND before your final message; commit source.
